posts.author: rex
posts.text: Lumen going from $9 to $14? That's a 55% jump for a note app. Apple Notes and Obsidian are free and do the job.

posts.author: dana
posts.text: I'll defend it: I'd pay $14 if sync got faster, and the team has been listening on that. Cheap compared to the hours I spend in it.

posts.author: priya

posts.author: theo

posts.author: dana
posts.text: rex, fair, 'cheap for my hours' only works if the product earns it. I'm still saying the team should announce faster sync before the bump, not after.

posts.author: rex

posts.text: Week two on Free and I haven't missed Pro once. theo, if sync speed isn't your thing, $14 is hard to justify.

posts.author: priya
posts.text: The Obsidian trial is going okay with my two teammates so far. Unless Lumen shows me something concrete, $14 a seat is a hard sell.

posts.author: kenji
posts.text: Moved my notes to a free app and it's fine. Thanks dana for the tips, but I can't justify $14 on my budget.

posts.author: dana
posts.text: kenji, totally get it, a student budget is a student budget. I still think the team needs to announce faster sync before the bump, otherwise it's just a bigger bill.

posts.author: rex
posts.text: priya, two teammates fine on Obsidian is the whole story. Nobody has shown me one thing Lumen does that free apps don't.

posts.author: priya
posts.text: rex, I'll give you this: the trial is holding up. But I'd still look at a demo if Lumen showed what the extra $5 a seat buys.

posts.author: theo
posts.text: marisol, sync speed is exactly my thing, so I'm staying on Pro for now. If $14 lands without faster sync, I'm reconsidering.

posts.author: marisol
posts.text: theo, fair, if sync is your bottleneck it makes sense. Mine isn't, so I'm staying on Free unless something new shows up.

context:
# notes
Lumen is a note-taking app that syncs across Mac, iPhone and the web.
Plans today: Free, and Pro at $9 a month.
Most users found Lumen through word of mouth; many compare it with free note apps.
Faster sync is the most requested improvement.
Insiders only: offline mode is in development, planned for the next release.
hypothesis: Lumen raised its plan from $9 to $14 a month?
name: lumen-raised-plan

findings.text: Willingness to pay hinges on faster sync. Dana and theo would accept $14 only if sync visibly improves, and both want it announced before the bump, not after.
Free alternatives (Apple Notes, Obsidian) were the main competitive anchor. Rex, kenji and marisol found no gap in free tools, and marisol didn't miss Pro after two weeks.
Priya, who buys per seat, is persuadable but unconvinced. Her Obsidian trial is holding up, yet she'd consider a demo showing what the extra $5 per seat buys.

report.headline: The $14 price drew resistance: price-sensitive users drifted to free apps while supporters demanded faster sync as justification.
questions: Does a measurable sync speed improvement, announced before the price change, convert conditional users like theo and dana into willing payers at $14?
Would a demo or team-tier justification for the extra $5 per seat keep multi-seat buyers like priya from moving to Obsidian?
